newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Daqing to maintain oil output until 2010.
newsitem.headline: China's Daqing to maintain oil output until 2010.

text.p: China's Daqing oilfield in the northeast plans to sink 47,000 new wells to maintain annual output at 50 million tonnes until the year 2010, the official Xinhua news agency said on Monday.
The agency's report, quoting Ding Guiming, director of the Daqing Petroleum Administration, did not say how much money would be needed to maintain output at 50 million tonnes a year.
Daqing, China's major oilfield, is relatively old and has been forced to rely on increasingly expensive tertiary recovery techniques to maintain production.
Daqing has proven oil reserves of 5.26 billion tonnes. It has produced 1.35 billion tonnes of crude oil since it began production in 1959.
The Daqing administration would also be active in natural gas exploration in other parts of China and in foreign countries, Ding said without elaborating.
